title: Is this fine? Haunted House 3D Game Environmental Asset
author: Haman24
selftext: I'm fairly new to 3d modeling and game design, I have been using Rapid Assets to create environmental assets, so something for the background that doesn't need to have interior. I really like the skin and texture of this model I think it did very well but the mesh is a little rough around the edges. But does that matter? I dont think it does but let me know what you think

comments.author: RUSuper
comments.body: I think it depends on how close camera will be to your house? From a far it would look amazing, but as you look at it closer you can see textures being washed out a bit and mesh problems. So if it is some sort of FPS game where players can get up to the house close I would push for better model and textures (maybe more polygons, maybe 8K or 4K textures etc) if it is from camera like isometric RTS style, this is good enough.

replies.author: Haman24
replies.body: Thanks for the guidance, I think for buildings where the player needs to get close I'll go for simpler designs so there's less need for iterations

replies.author: Original-League-6094
replies.body: For buildings where the player gets close, you really need modular designs because you will probably iterate quite a bit.

comments.author: Xylozene
comments.body: No it looks like absolute shit, why are there decks for windows that have no doors? Tf gang did you even look at it

comments.author: DarkShiftInteractive
comments.body: If you’re new then you should learn blender and 3d modeling instead of using ai that gives you no control of geometry whatsoever and gives your high poly low quality assets, I’d recommend learning blender & probuilder (if using Unity) instead of working to ship something experimental
